claims.text: Conventional metal substrates such as steel or similar alloys are used for sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
These conventional metal components are prone to rapid corrosion during exposure to molten aluminum.
A dense TiB2 ceramic layer can be deposited on the metal parts by physical vapor deposition or plasma spraying.
The deposited TiB2 layer is non-wetting toward molten aluminum.
The TiB2 coating forms a continuous and adherent barrier on the metal substrate.
TiB2 is chemically inert under exposure to high-temperature molten aluminum.
The TiB2 barrier isolates the underlying metal from direct contact with molten aluminum.
TiB2 is thermally stable under the stated hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
The TiB2 layer limits molten-aluminum wetting and reactive contact with the underlying metal.
The TiB2 layer minimizes penetration of aluminum into the substrate.
Limiting wetting, penetration, and reactive contact reduces corrosion and erosion of the metal component.
TiB2-coated components will experience significantly less erosion and chemical attack than uncoated components.
Reduced erosion and chemical attack will extend the service life of TiB2-coated components relative to uncoated parts.
The protective effect depends on the coating remaining dense, adherent, and intact under operational thermal and mechanical stresses.
Coating defects or failure under extreme conditions may diminish protection against molten aluminum.
The magnitude of erosion reduction and service-life improvement depends on coating quality, thickness, and adhesion.
